teamInfo.title: What is a team memory?
teamInfo.what: A team memory is an agent memory folder shared with a team. What one teammate's agent learns — project decisions, how a service works, gotchas — every teammate's agent can recall. Your personal memory stays yours.
teamInfo.when: Agents save to your personal memory unless you ask them to remember something for the team. Then they write to the team memory. If you can write to more than one, they use the one you pick below; with none picked, the agent has to name one each time.
teamInfo.setup: To set one up: make a folder an agent memory (⋯ → “{{useAsMemory}}”), share it with your team as editors (⋯ → {{share}} → turn on {{public}}, then add the team under {{editors}}), then pick it below.

memory.splitterHint: What agents remember is split into small cards with summaries and links. The text, plus the titles and summaries of related cards, is sent to the provider you choose.
memory.noProviders: Add an AI provider (AI panel) on this server to use this.
memory.entityNotesHint: Notes and memory cards about this
memory.brainHint: Projects glow as hubs, cards orbit them, and signals run along their links — brightest where knowledge crosses between projects. Click a card to open it, a project to zoom in.

brainHelp.title: Turn on Brain
brainHelp.intro: Brain shows what your AI agents remember, as a living graph.
brainHelp.connect: Connect your AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor…) to PatchMan in {{path}}.
brainHelp.remember: As it works, the agent saves what it learns as cards in an “Agent Memory” folder, created on its first save. You can also make one of your own folders a memory: in {{myNotes}}, open its ⋯ menu → “{{useAsMemory}}”.
brainHelp.view: Open the memory folder and switch the view to “{{brain}}” to see the cards as a graph.
brainHelp.team: Optional: share the memory folder with your team as editors to build a team brain — what one agent learns, every teammate's agent can recall.
